# Managing AI and human agents: The contact center supervisor’s new reality


by


[Yael Stanger Sonsino](https://www.nice.com/blog/author/yael-stanger-sonsino)


October 14, 2026


| Updated: October 20, 2026


Share

On any given day, a contact center supervisor is watching service levels, checking queues, helping agents through difficult conversations, coaching people who need support, and stepping in before customer problems get worse.


Now, add AI agents to the team.


These agents handle customer interactions themselves. That fundamentally changes the supervisor's job.


[Gartner's April 2026 research](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-04-28-gartner-identifies-six-steps-to-manage-artificial-intelligence-agent-sprawl) predicts that by 2028, the average global Fortune 500 enterprise will use more than 150,000 AI agents, up from fewer than 15 in 2025.[Metrigy's 2026 research](https://www.techtarget.com/enterprise-software/tip/AI-self-service-benefits-and-best-practices) found that AI fully resolves 29.2% of customer interactions today, and companies expect that share to reach 60% by 2030. Gartner's April 2026 research also found that only 13% of organizations think they have the right AI agent governance in place.


In the contact center, that gap lands on the supervisor. Supervisors were already responsible for service levels, queues, coaching, and stepping in before customer problems get worse. Many are now also expected to oversee AI agents that handle customer interactions on their own.


Customers will still need human agents for complex, sensitive, and high-value moments. Human agents will still need coaching and support. And when a customer moves between AI and a person, they experience a single company, no matter which part of the workforce handled each step of the journey.


Contact center supervisors need to lead one workforce.


For executives, the stakes go beyond efficiency.


**Accountability:** when a customer's journey crosses between AI and people, someone has to own the outcome, and that takes shared visibility.


**Resolution:** a contained interaction only counts if the customer's issue was resolved, so leaders need to see where and why AI hands over.


**Resilience:** when an AI flow starts to underperform, the operation must spot it and respond before customers feel it.


Meeting this challenge is what[NiCE Supervisor](https://www.nice.com/products/supervisor-workspace) is being built for: giving supervisors the visibility, intelligence, and control to manage human and AI agents together, without asking one person to somehow watch everything at once.


## The contact center supervisor’s world just got bigger


A simple problem sits inside the hybrid workforce: most organizations were built to manage a different kind of workforce.


Organizations have traditionally managed human agents through one set of workforce processes. Automation has lived somewhere else. AI agents have introduced another layer of monitoring, data, and operational responsibility.


That separation becomes harder to sustain when all three contribute to the same customer journey.


A supervisor might need to know whether a human agent is available, whether an AI agent's containment rate is dropping, whether sentiment is deteriorating across a group of interactions, why customers are being handed over to human agents, and whether an emerging problem requires a person to step in.


If those answers live in different places, the supervisor becomes the integration layer.


That's exactly what technology should prevent.


The answer is one operating model for human and AI work, with shared visibility, unified performance signals, measurable handoffs, and a clear path from insight to action.


NiCE Supervisor puts that idea into practice, bringing together the new Supervisor Workspace and Copilot for Supervisors as part of a unified CX AI platform.


## One view of the whole workforce


The first requirement of hybrid supervision sounds obvious: supervisors need to see the workforce they're managing.


NiCE Supervisor brings human and AI activity into a shared management experience.


The benefit is a clearer view of what's happening across the customer experience and where a supervisor's attention can make the greatest difference. Through Supervisor Workspace, supervisors can see active contacts, SLA, sentiment, queue health, and containment across human and AI agents in one customizable experience.


The goal is to help supervisors understand the state of the customer experience, which takes more than side-by-side human and AI metrics.


For human agents, supervisors can monitor voice and digital interactions, view capacity, coach in the moment, and step into an interaction when needed.


For AI agents, supervisors need a different kind of visibility. They need to know whether the AI is achieving the intended outcome, where it's struggling, when it hands customers over to human agents, and whether an issue requires human judgment.


The measures may differ, but they all contribute to one customer experience.


#### A hybrid workforce solution needs one way to understand how every agent contributes to the customer outcome.


## Know where human attention matters


Seeing everything creates its own problem: there is too much to see.


Supervisors today may already be responsible for dozens of people and hundreds of interactions across multiple channels. Add AI agents operating continuously at machine speed, and the traditional model of monitoring individual contacts reaches its limit.


Supervisors become more effective when something helps them find the moments that call for a person.


This is where Copilot for Supervisors changes the experience.


Supervisors can get on-demand summaries of active interactions, giving them immediate context without having to listen from the beginning. Intent-based alerts can detect conversations based on meaning, rather than requiring someone to anticipate every possible keyword. Urgent Assist can surface interactions that need attention so supervisors can decide whether to monitor, join, or assist.


Each alert is triggered by signals in the conversation itself, such as intent, sentiment, or urgency, and arrives with the reason it fired and a running summary, so the supervisor can judge quickly whether to step in.


The supervisor persona is being fundamentally redefined: instead of asking, "Where am I needed?", supervisors can increasingly rely on AI to offload workload and tell them when their attention is needed, so they could start asking "What else can I do now?" and focus their time and judgment where they can have the greatest impact.


## See the pattern, not just the interaction


The next step is moving beyond individual contacts altogether.


Imagine containment begins dropping across a set of AI-led interactions. A dashboard can show you the number, but the number is only a symptom. Something caused it.


Maybe customers are repeatedly struggling with the same part of a journey. Maybe a particular intent is producing unexpected results. Maybe a handoff is happening too late. Maybe sentiment is falling across interactions that appear unrelated when viewed one at a time.


NiCE's hybrid supervisor solution within the new Agentic Workspace platform* is designed to surface those kinds of patterns.


Agentic Supervisors can work continuously in the background, monitoring interactions, detecting trends, and escalating situations that require human attention. The human supervisor has complete visibility into the decisions and autonomous actions of Agentic Supervisors, with the ability to drill down, investigate, flag areas for improvement, or even revert actions altogether, maintaining complete control.


Autonomous action stays visible.


Agentic Supervisors handle simple tasks, freeing humans for the most complex issues. The Agentic Activity section shows supervisors what these agents are doing.


When something requires human attention, it can surface for review rather than disappear into an automated process.


That combination is what counts: automation where it helps, transparency where it's needed, and human control when judgment is required.


## Turn insight into action


Finding an issue matters most when the supervisor can understand it and act on it.


When supervisors drill into an AI-led interaction, NiCE's hybrid monitoring experience gives them visibility into the live interaction and the AI flow behind it, including the interaction's current status and what happened previously.


From there, the supervisor can respond based on what the situation requires.


If the AI flow needs improvement, they can make changes themselves (if authorized) or flag it to the designated AI Ops owner for review. If the customer needs a person, the interaction can be reassigned to a human skill or specific agent. And when the situation demands direct intervention, the supervisor can take over.


When an interaction moves to a person, the context moves with it: the receiving agent or supervisor can see what the AI flow has already done and where the customer stands, so nobody starts from zero.


Together, these create a much more meaningful model for human oversight, one built on the supervisor's judgment rather than on approving each step.


Intelligence can monitor broadly, identify patterns, and bring forward context. The human supervisor can understand the situation, decide what to prioritize, and act.


Consider a retailer during a major product launch. The AI agent is successfully handling order-status inquiries, but in real time, the supervisor notices a sudden spike in customers asking about delayed deliveries because of an unexpected shipping disruption. The AI is still following its existing flow, but the interaction data reveals that customers now need a different response, including proactive reassurance and information about the delay.


Rather than waiting for CSAT to decline, the supervisor can flag the relevant AI flow in real time and request an adjustment to reflect the new situation. Within the same operational window, the AI agent can begin responding with the updated information, helping reduce customer frustration and protect CSAT.


This is where real-time visibility becomes particularly powerful: supervisors are not just monitoring AI performance; they are using live customer signals to continuously adapt how AI responds to what is happening in the business.


## Make handoffs measurable


Another part of the hybrid workforce, the space between AI and humans, deserves much more attention.


An AI agent might handle most of a customer journey successfully and then hand the interaction to a person.


Was that a successful AI interaction?


Answering requires knowing why the handoff happened, whether it happened at the right moment, how long the customer then waited, whether the human received enough context, what happened to handle time, and ultimately whether the customer got the outcome they needed.


NiCE treats handoffs as a measurable part of performance.


Performance Management can bring together measures such as handoff volume, handle time, and CSAT across AI and human portions of the journey. AI agents also need measures specific to their work, including containment, fallback, and intent accuracy.


The goal is to create aligned measures that show how humans and AI each contribute to the same customer and business outcome, with scorecards that reflect the different work each one does.


Aligned measures like these are what managing one workforce means.


## Give contact supervisors more space to lead


It is tempting to imagine the future supervisor sitting in front of an enormous command center, watching every human agent, AI agent, metric, and customer interaction.


Supervisors are people leaders.


Their real value comes from judgment, experience, empathy, and the ability to recognize when an agent needs coaching, when a customer needs a person, when a pattern signals a bigger problem, and when the operation needs to change course.


Technology should increase capacity for more of these moments, not bury supervisors.


The bigger story behind NiCE Supervisor is the platform around it, a unified CX AI platform where interactions, human agents, AI agents, performance signals and workflows can inform one another. That same unified operating model extends across workforce management, quality, performance, and the broader workforce experience.


When something changes, the goal is to understand what happened, surface what needs attention, help the right person act, learn from the outcome, and improve the next experience.


## One workforce needs one way to lead


As AI agents and human teams work more closely together, the supervisor’s role is even more consequential.


AI agents can operate at a scale no supervisor could personally monitor. Human agents will increasingly handle complex situations that require empathy and judgment. Customers will move between the two expecting a connected experience, with context preserved and responsibility clear.


Supervisors will be responsible for making that collaboration work. They need a clear view of performance, automation they can direct, and shared service goals supported by measures suited to each type of agent. They also need to recognize when automation can continue independently and when a person should take the lead.


The hybrid workforce changes what supervisors manage. NiCE Supervisor changes what they can see, understand, and do about it.


When humans and AI serve the same customer, a shared dashboard is the best way to start and a unified way to work takes it to the next level.

This requires shared visibility, clear accountability, and coordinated workflows. Human judgment remains central to deciding when to intervene, support an employee, or adjust how the operation serves customers.

A supervisor can inspect the live interaction and its AI flow, then adjust the flow if authorized, flag it to the designated AI Ops owner, reassign the interaction, or take over directly. When the interaction moves to a human skill, specific agent, or supervisor, its context moves with it, allowing the receiving person to see what the AI has done and where the customer stands.


Contact centers should measure AI-to-human handoffs by examining why they occur, their timing, customer wait time, context transfer, handle time, and the final customer outcome. Handoff volume, handle time, and CSAT help connect performance across the AI and human portions of a journey. AI-specific measures, including containment, fallback, and intent accuracy, add operational detail.
